body:
Parent: #22 (Evidence & Data Trust).

## Traceability and dependencies
Requirements: FR-01, FR-02 (defined in parent epic breakdown).
Depends on: #34

## Outcome
Every source-derived field emitted by extraction points to inspectable captured evidence or explicitly explains why support is unavailable.

## Scope and technical plan
- Carry capture context through `_extract.py`, extractor adapters and `_normalize.py` using the approved evidence contract.
- Cover current API, feed, unified/structured-data, CSS and optional LLM paths. Capture actual response/page URLs and observed times; retain only bounded relevant source fragments or pointer-resolvable structured data.
- Record normalization transformations (including GTIN restoration) without replacing original observations; reuse existing `_identifier_sources` and `_identifier_normalization` where meaningful.
- Link variants and nested collections to correct source items; do not reuse a parent value as variant evidence or mistake a product URL for the fetched API URL.
- Unsupported adapters/fields must explicitly report unsupported reasons rather than fabricate excerpts or timestamps. A pointer is useful only with retained data, not merely a live page.

## Acceptance scenarios
- Given API, feed, structured HTML, CSS and mocked LLM fixtures, when extracted, then every emitted factual field satisfies the contract coverage audit.
- Given LLM output with no supporting source span/pointer, then the field is unsupported and cannot acquire validated confidence from the model score.
- Given normalized or enriched identifiers, then both the original evidence and transformation explanation are inspectable.
- Given absent versus explicit zero/false source values, then provenance preserves the distinction through normalization.

## Validation and task handoff
Offline fixtures for each extraction family and variant mapping; regression checks for identifiers, stock, currency and extraction errors. Define bounded capture limits and truncation behavior in `plan.md` and public documentation.

## Spec Kit workflow
Use one shared feature directory, `specs/002-evidence-data-trust/`. Specify user outcomes and Given/When/Then scenarios in `spec.md`; record architecture, compatibility and resolved questions in `plan.md`; maintain dependency-ordered, requirement-linked work in `tasks.md`. Update the relevant artifacts before implementation and verify spec/plan/tasks consistency before closing this ticket. These are required implementation deliverables, not artifacts already generated by an installed Spec Kit workflow.

## Boundaries and definition of done
Evidence-backed reporting only; no catalog mutations, MCP, webhooks, or other epic work. Preserve MIT licensing and self-hostability. Prefer deterministic, offline fixtures; no model launch or broad live crawl is required. Document public APIs and limitations, and run meaningful affected compatibility checks. Do not equate extraction quality, rule/model scores, and validated confidence.

comments.body:
Implemented and pushed in PR #42: https://github.com/umerkhan95/shopextract/pull/42

The PR is ready for review and stacked on foundation PR #41 (#34). This ticket remains open until the changes reach main; merge #41 first and retarget #42 to main.

Acceptance coverage:
- API, feed, structured HTML, CSS and mocked LLM fields receive inspectable retained evidence or explicit unsupported reasons.
- Shared normalization selections/conversion outcomes prevent default zero prices, unknown conditions and fallback images from acquiring incorrect observed support.
- Correct platform-specific variant mappings, original identifier evidence/transformation history, fetched redirect URLs and UTC capture times.
- Bounded capture: 4 KiB fragments and 64 KiB retained source payload per product. LLM scores do not become validated confidence.
- All five reported P2 findings have regression coverage.
- Spec/plan/tasks/public documentation and verification summaries updated.

The requested storefront follow-up is included: native Magento GraphQL, Shopware Store API, BigCommerce GraphQL and documentation-based authentication mocks. BigCommerce supports storefront/private/impersonation modes and strict customer-session handling. The mock executes the actual query against documented field types/nullability and tests rejection, redaction, pagination and partial failures. A live Magento final-page truncation/completeness bug was also reproduced and fixed.

Validation: 535 offline tests passed; focused storefront/auth suite 91 passed; 18 live stress cases passed across all six supported platform families and seven sites. Magento full-catalog probe returned 181 products and 1,847 variants. git diff --check passed. Counts and limitations are documented in the PR reports; no authenticated live BigCommerce catalog claim is made.

Evidence-resolution/persistence/export follow-up tickets are not completed by this PR.
